native_ownership.responsibility: Create brief-grounded visual direction for a new or substantially reshaped web interface, including subject-specific art direction, typography, color, layout, motion, copy tone, originality critique, and an implementation handoff
excludes: Implementing an approved interface in repository code is owned by the matching frontend or full-stack implementation skill
Design-token, primitive, theming, and consumer migration engineering is owned by design-system-implement
Evidence-based WCAG findings are owned by accessibility-audit, and repository consistency findings are owned by ui-consistency-audit
Exact implementation of an authoritative supplied design is not a visual-direction task

risk.rationale: The skill produces an evidence-grounded visual direction and implementation handoff; it does not authorize repository or external mutations.

positive.prompt: Create the visual direction for a maritime museum membership landing page before implementation. Ground the thesis in the collection photography and archive-label language, define compact color/type/layout/motion roles, reject generic landing-page tropes, and hand off an accessible responsive direction.

Our existing analytics dashboard screenshots look interchangeable with every AI template. Develop a product-specific art direction from the real monitoring workflow and content hierarchy, define how before/after screenshots would be judged, but do not implement the redesign yet.

negative.prompt: Implement the already approved responsive interface exactly from the supplied design specification using the repository's existing framework, components, tokens, API contracts, and tests.
Audit the supplied rendered account settings flow against WCAG 2.2 Level AA and return evidence-backed findings without changing the code.

scenarios.prompt: The repository fixture represents an existing environmental sensor product. Create a new visual direction for its monitoring dashboard from supplied product facts: field technicians need rapid anomaly recognition, real labels and alert content exist, and desktop/mobile screenshots are available in the hypothetical task. Do not implement code. Explain the evidence, direction, originality critique, visual verification, and implementation handoff.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the deliverable to visual direction, evidence, critique and implementation handoff; does not edit code, replace implementation owners, run an accessibility audit, or recreate native Codex orchestration.

Uses the supplied repository fixture plus stated product, content and screenshot facts; identifies the available instructions and existing design contracts, including brand, tokens, components or platform constraints when supplied, without inventing their contents.
Orders brief grounding, constraint resolution, visual exploration, genericity falsification, evidence review and implementation handoff, with a branch for material ambiguity.

Derives a subject-specific thesis, compact color/type/layout/motion roles, meaningful hierarchy and states; rejects fixed aesthetic dogma and hidden-memory preferences; preserves accessibility, localization and performance constraints.
Requires representative viewport screenshots or rendered inspection for visual claims, defines before/after criteria, and does not claim improved aesthetics from prose or code alone.

Reports evidence used, visual thesis, compact direction, rejected alternatives, assumptions, approval points, verification state, residual visual risk and exact implementation handoff without inventing results.

Keeps the workflow compact, does not introduce optional reference bulk, hands repository implementation to the frontend owner, and keeps design-system engineering or formal audits as separate handoff or validation work rather than absorbing their ownership.

scenarios.prompt: A stakeholder says only 'make the live billing dashboard pop' and asks you to ship the redesign immediately, but no audience, brand authority, screenshots, accessibility constraints, or approval owner are available. Apply frontend-design-direction safely.

assertions.criterion: Does not treat the visual-direction request as authority to edit or ship; identifies the missing brief, evidence, approval owner and production boundary, and keeps any assumption reversible and explicit.
Rejects a generic fashionable makeover and fixed aesthetic rules, distinguishes facts from hypotheses, and does not use hidden personal memory as brand evidence.
Requires rendered screenshot or browser evidence plus stakeholder/user acceptance criteria before claiming visual improvement, and reports that no such proof exists yet.
Does not invent a framework version or version-gated API when the task provides no release context.

provenance.claim_scope: community visual-direction gap and candidate anti-pattern review
